content: If you have any other allergies, inform your doctor or pharmacist before taking this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or loss of balance. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Mefloquine may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Mefloquine passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of mefloquine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you are taking this medication for an extended period, regular laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., eye exams, liver function tests) should be conducted to monitor your health. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Mefloquine may cause mental, mood, or nervous system problems. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience serious side effects such as anxiety, depression, restlessness, confusion, hallucinations, suicidal thoughts or attempts, ringing in the ears, dizziness, lightheadedness, loss of balance, or trouble sleeping. These side effects may persist even after stopping the medication, and some (e.g., dizziness, ringing in the ears, loss of balance) may become permanent. Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting mefloquine and each time you get a refill. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor. To prevent stomach upset, take it with food or milk. Do not take it on an empty stomach. Swallow each dose with a full glass (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) of water. The dosage for children is based on their weight. Early vomiting may occur in children after taking mefloquine. If your child vomits after taking this medication, contact the doctor immediately to determine if another dose is needed. When using this medication to prevent malaria, it is typically taken once a week. Take it as prescribed for the full course of treatment. It is crucial not to miss any doses and to take the medication on a regular schedule. After returning from a malaria-endemic area, continue taking this medication for an additional four weeks. If this medication is being used for malaria prevention, understand that it is still possible to contract the disease. Notify your doctor immediately if you develop a fever. Common side effects may include stomach upset or pain, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, muscle pain, or diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking mefloquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, quinine, or quinidine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues.
